verdict: Caution: lend selectively to branded, compliant plywood and laminate units with verified timber sourcing and clean banking; avoid traders and units with unhedged import exposure or diversion risk.
title: Yamunanagar Plywood, Veneer & Laminates: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Plywood is a timber-conversion business: face veneer, core timber and chemicals go in, and cash comes out only after seasoning, pressing, grading and dispatch.** Value sits in the veneer and core timber stock and in the brand on the finished sheet; cash sits in the working-capital cycle between timber purchase and dealer realisation. Rating commentary flags input price volatility and import dependence in select timber as the core risk [8], and Greenply's ratings note that adequate raw-material availability near the plant is a key driver [10]. So when a proposal lands, check where the unit buys veneer and core timber and at what distance; if sourcing is spot-market and distant, ask for the last twelve months of purchase invoices by supplier. Peer results are mixed: Greenlam's plywood segment grew 90.7% YoY in one quarter [4] and 22.2% YoY in Q2FY26 [6], while laminates volume fell 7% YoY in another quarter [5]. The data pack shows India-wide IIP for NIC 16 at +8.6% YoY but -0.8% Apr-to-date [D], and bank credit +20.6% YoY against that output [D]. **Credit is running far ahead of output, so the risk is lending into inventory, not into demand.**

## Where the growth is
**Haryana GST collections are running +10.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], so the local trade channel is absorbing stock faster than the national average.** Pursue branded laminate and value-added board makers selling to dealers and interior projects, and plywood units with own veneer peeling and a compliance paper trail. Avoid pure traders, units with no own seasoning or pressing capacity, and anyone whose pitch is cheap imported timber. The rating view is that formalisation and brand-led share gains favour premium laminates and compliant boards [8]. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the timber cycle, not the balance sheet.** Keep tenor short and matched to the stock-and-receivable cycle, take stock and receivable statements monthly, and take GST returns monthly against bank statements. Ask for a hedging policy where imports exist, since rating commentary flags exchange-rate exposure on imported raw material [11]. Where the customer cannot give a timber sourcing map, collect from customer. ## Early-warning signs
- **Cheap-raw-material offers or sudden supplier changes** -> stop disbursement and inspect godown stock. - **GST turnover falling below bank credits for two months** -> freeze limit enhancement. - **Receivable days stretching beyond the stated cycle** -> ask for dealer-wise ageing. - **Unhedged import payables rising** -> seek cover or reduce exposure.
watch: GST turnover below bank credits for two months -> freeze enhancement and inspect stock
Receivable days stretch beyond stated cycle -> ask for dealer-wise ageing and re-rate limit
Shift to spot or distant suppliers -> require sourcing map and re-price risk
Unhedged payables rise -> seek cover or cut exposure
